newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end up a tad,led by brewing giant.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end up a tad,led by brewing giant.

text.p: Colombian stocks rose Friday, fueled by small investor demand for brewing giant Bavaria, in markets that failed to shake off holiday season torpor.

Bogota's IBB index edged up 0.29 percent to 846.92 amid a 262 million peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index made a wafer-thin 0.02 percent gain to close at 13,469.27 amid a 492 million peso volume.
"There's emerging demand for Bavaria because of recent announcements on investments and joint ventures planned for 1997," one Bogota broker said.
Bavaria, the mainstay of the Santo Domingo industrial conglomerate, climbed 2.31 percent to 4,195 on the Bogot exchange. In Medelln, it rose 2.44 percent to 4,200.

At the end of last year, Bavaria announced it would sell 55 percent of Bancoqua bank, the financial arm of the Santo Domingo group, to Spain's Grupo Santander. It also announced a joint venture with French supermarket chain Carrefour and a joint investment with British Petroleum Co Plc in a thermal generating plant.
"Bavaria has succeeded in boosting its image," a Medelln broker said.
The other main gain of the day in Medelln was a 1.61 percent rise in supermarket chain Almacenes Exito, which closed at 3,150 amid a 220 million peso trade.
